etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English felynge, equivalent to feel +‎ -ing.

definitions.definition: Expressive of great sensibility; attended by, or evincing, sensibility.

quote.citation: 2022 January 12, Paul Bigland, “Fab Four: the nation's finest stations: London Bridge”, in RAIL, number 948, page 31:
quote.text: Part of the 'western arcade' (as it's known) is lined with delis, cafes and other shops, giving it the feeling of a bazaar.

definitions.definition: (always in the plural) Emotional state or well-being.
(always in the plural) Emotional attraction or desire.

quote.citation: 1987, “Fairytale of New York”, performed by The Pogues:
quote.text: Got on a lucky one / Came in eighteen to one / I've got a feeling / This year's for me and you

quote.citation: 1972, George J. W. Goodman (Adam Smith), Supermoney, page 156:
quote.text: When you are tempted to speculate in cocoa, lie down until the feeling goes away.

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of feel
